description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:153-168

```rust
pub struct SctVerifier<V: SignatureVerifier> {
    logs: CtLogList,
    verifier: V,
}

impl<V: SignatureVerifier> SctVerifier<V> {
    pub const fn new(logs: CtLogList, verifier: V) -> Self { ... }
    pub const fn logs(&self) -> &CtLogList { &self.logs }
}
```

The struct is constructed once and never mutated. Callers cannot:

- Update the log list as new logs are added to Chrome's log_list.json
  feed (real production servers refresh this weekly).
- Recover the inner `V` to reuse it with a different log list (some
  verifier impls hold expensive state like pre-loaded keys).
- Swap the log list while holding the same `&SctVerifier` reference
  (typical pattern for ArcSwap-backed live config).

The contract is: build once at startup, never refresh. That's a real
production limitation. A long-running TLS server that wants to honor
log retirement events has to:

1. Construct a new `SctVerifier`
2. Atomically swap the `Arc<SctVerifier>` in their config slot
3. Old connections finish on the old verifier; new connections use
   the new one

…which is fine, but it requires the caller to wrap `SctVerifier` in
ArcSwap or RwLock themselves. The crate provides no accessor that
would let the caller mutate-in-place even if they hold the only
reference.

Recommendation: add accessors:

```rust
impl<V: SignatureVerifier> SctVerifier<V> {
    pub fn logs_mut(&mut self) -> &mut CtLogList { &mut self.logs }
    pub fn replace_logs(&mut self, new: CtLogList) -> CtLogList { ... }
    pub fn into_parts(self) -> (CtLogList, V) { (self.logs, self.verifier) }
}
```

Cost: 3 short methods. Benefit: callers can refresh in-place or
recover the inner verifier.

Priority P3: workaround (build new + swap Arc) exists; this is
ergonomic improvement.

Non-negotiable #6 is also relevant here: callbacks-not-closed-structs
implies the caller can wrap. If the caller wants to wrap with a
fresh-log-list closure they can already implement `SignatureVerifier`
themselves and inject log_list lookup at the verifier layer. So
this is API ergonomics, not framework violation.
title: SctVerifier::logs() returns &CtLogList — no way to swap log list, drop verifier, or recover V
